name: aphasia syndromes overview
title: Cortical syndromes: test comprehension first, then fluency and repetition; the pattern names the aphasia and localizes it in the dominant hemisphere (Broca's inferior frontal, Wernicke's posterior temporal, global full MCA territory; conduction and the transcortical aphasias for keeners); neglect points to the non-dominant hemisphere, and apraxia, cortical sensory signs and extinction also localize to the cortex

root.title: Trouble with LANGUAGE (aphasia), not articulation (dysarthria)?
lines: aphasia = DOMINANT hemisphere (left in right-handers) · dominant MCA stroke usually has some
matters: an aphasic patient is NOT confused or delirious
test naming · comprehension · fluency · repetition · reading · writing
comprehension: MOTOR commands, 1 → 3 step · fluency: nonsense sounds still = fluent · repetition: "no ifs, ands or buts"

head: h

clue: • like a foreign language if severe

panels.title: Non-dominant hemisphere: neglect
items: visual neglect: ignores one side · blink to threat may stay
sensory neglect: ignores touch on one side
asomatognosia: own body part not recognized
dressing apraxia: can't put clothes on

panels.title: Other cortical signs
items: apraxia: can't do a motor task DESPITE power · parietal or frontal
e.g. pretend hammer, hand postures, dressing, whistle, draw
cortical sensory (primary intact): graphesthesia, stereognosis, direction
primary sensory loss can't localize to cortex
extinction: misses one side only when BOTH stimulated · touch → parietal, vision → occipital

panels.title: Localization pearls
items: CORTEX: aphasia, neglect, apraxia, cortical sensory · homonymous hemianopia
SUBCORTICAL: pure motor or pure sensory face + arm + leg · ataxic hemiparesis
BRAINSTEM: vertigo or diplopia PLUS another symptom · crossed face vs body sensory
